mcqs.question: Which of the following lists the metals in order of decreasing reactivity as given in the general reactivity series?

options.A: Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc, Iron, Nickel, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold
options.B: Sodium, Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium, Zinc, Aluminium, Iron, Nickel, Lead, Tin, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold
options.C: Potassium, Calcium, Sodium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc, Iron, Nickel, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold
options.D: Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Zinc, Aluminium, Iron, Nickel, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold

mcqs.answer: Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc, Iron, Nickel, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Silver, Gold
mcqs.explanation: The NCERT general reactivity series (most to least reactive) is: Potassium > Sodium > Calcium > Magnesium > Aluminium > Zinc > Iron > Nickel > Tin > Lead > Hydrogen > Copper > Silver > Gold. Option A follows this exact order, while the other options have misplaced elements.

mcqs.question: Which metal will displace copper from an aqueous solution of copper(II) sulfate?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so it can replace Cu²⁺ ions in CuSO₄ solution, forming ZnSO₄ and depositing copper metal. Iron can also displace copper, but the most straightforward answer among the options is zinc. Silver and gold are less reactive than copper and cannot displace it.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: When iron filings are added to copper(II) sulfate solution, which observation is expected?

options.B: Deposition of copper metal and the solution turns pale green
options.C: Formation of a black precipitate of iron(III) oxide

mcqs.answer: Deposition of copper metal and the solution turns pale green
mcqs.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces Cu²⁺ ions. Copper metal precipitates as a reddish-brown solid, and iron(II) sulfate formed gives the solution a pale green colour. No gas is evolved and no black oxide forms under these conditions.

mcqs.question: Metal A is placed in a solution of metal B's salt and metal B is placed in a solution of metal A's salt. Metal A displaces metal B from its salt solution, but metal B does not displace metal A from its solution. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Metal A is higher in the reactivity series than metal B
options.B: Metal B is higher in the reactivity series than metal A
options.D: No conclusion can be drawn from the experiment

mcqs.answer: Metal A is higher in the reactivity series than metal B
mcqs.explanation: A metal can displace another only if it is more reactive. Since A displaces B but B cannot displace A, A must be higher (more reactive) than B in the series.

mcqs.question: Identify the misconception: "Gold is more reactive than zinc because gold reacts readily with acids."

options.C: Both parts of the statement are true
options.D: Both parts of the statement are false

mcqs.explanation: Gold is actually the least reactive metal in the series; it does not react with most acids. Zinc is much more reactive and can displace hydrogen from acids. Therefore the claim that gold is more reactive than zinc is incorrect.

mcqs.question: A metal X when added to aqueous silver nitrate solution gives a black precipitate of silver. What does this indicate about metal X in the reactivity series?

options.A: Metal X is less reactive than silver
options.B: Metal X is more reactive than silver
options.C: Metal X has the same reactivity as silver
options.D: No inference can be made about the reactivity

mcqs.answer: Metal X is more reactive than silver
mcqs.explanation: The formation of metallic silver indicates that X has displaced Ag⁺ ions from solution. Displacement occurs only when the added metal is higher (more reactive) than the metal ion being displaced. Hence X is more reactive than silver.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question:
Consider the two reactions:
(1) Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → Cu(s) + ZnSO₄(aq)
(2) Cu(s) + ZnSO₄(aq) → Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq)
Which reaction(s) will occur spontaneously under standard conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so it can displace Cu²⁺ ions, making reaction (1) spontaneous. Copper is lower than zinc and cannot displace Zn²⁺ ions; therefore reaction (2) does not occur spontaneously.

mcqs.question: In a competitive exam, which of the following metals will NOT displace any of the others from their aqueous salt solutions?
mcqs.explanation: Copper lies below iron, zinc and magnesium in the reactivity series, making it less reactive than all three. Hence it cannot displace any of them from their salt solutions, whereas the other metals can displace copper.
